title: Erin Patterson appeal live: mushroom murderer challenges convictions over fatal beef wellington lunch
text: 12m ago 21.36 EDT ‘Dangerous’ and ‘unfair’ phone tower evidence should not have been permitted, court hears Patterson’s defence barrister, Veronika Drago , says the mobile phone tower evidence and the death cap mushroom sightings posted to the citizen science website iNaturalist should not have been permitted in the trial. She says “objective evidence” about cell towers was turned into “subjective evidence” by expert witness Dr Matthew Sorell. Sorrell, a digital forensics science expert, analysed Patterson’s mobile phone records for police and testified at the trial. Drago says the judge, Justice Christopher Beale , ruled that the cell tower evidence did not prove that Patterson visited Outtrim and Loch – where sightings of the lethal death cap mushrooms were posted online to the platform iNaturalist. Drago says Beale said it only showed the possibility visited the locations on the dates raised in the trial. She says the cell tower evidence was “dangerous” and “unfair”. During the trial, fungi expert Dr Thomas May told the court that he uploaded a post on iNaturalist on 21 May 2023 identifying death cap mushrooms in Outtrim. title: Australia politics live: One Nation files three years of overdue financial returns hours before deadline
text: 20.14 EDT One Nation files three years of overdue financial returns Sarah Martin Pauline Hanson ’s One Nation party has complied with a request from the Queensland regulator to file three years of overdue financial returns. The party was sent a demand from the Office of Fair Trading (OFT) last month to submit the missing returns by 18 August or face compliance action. An OFT spokesperson told the Guardian on Wednesday that the returns were filed after business hours on Tuesday, ahead of the midnight deadline. They said: One Nation Queensland Division Inc has now lodged audited financial statements for the years 2022/2023, 2023/2024 and 2024/2025, as required by the Associations Incorporation Act 1981 . The Office of Fair Trading has notified One Nation Queensland Division Inc that any future failures to lodge annual returns within prescribed time limits may result in enforcement action. Pauline Hanson speaks to One Nation senators Sean Bell (right) and Tyron Whitten in March. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP Under the act, members of the management committee of an incorporated association must ensure financial statements are lodged for the association’s last reportable financial year. title: Tupac Shakur murder trial: ‘You better treat me as a hostile witness,’ Suge Knight associate testifies – as it happened
text: 20.23 EDT Closing summary The second day of the Tupac Shakur murder trial featured testimony from a wide range of witnesses, with a wide range of attitudes toward the legal process: Dr. Lisa Gavin, a medical examiner, reviewed the autopsy report and photos of Shakur’s body, and said that the evidence showed his death was a homicide. Some relatives of Shakur left the courtroom in response to the graphic photographs, while others looked away. Former Las Vegas police detective Dean O’Kelley described responding to the scene of Shakur’s shooting, spotting the bullet cases in the middle of the street, and using traffic cones to try to protect the crime scene until investigators arrived. “I told every attorney that tried to get me in here, you’d better treat me as a hostile witness,” James McDonald, an associate of Death Row Records co-founder Suge Knight, told the court, as he gave some details of reactions to Shakur’s shooting, but declined to answer other questions. “Me or anybody else bringing up the dead is wrong.”
author: Lois Beckett
